1.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A (2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention
of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection
order dated 20.02.2024 passed by the learned Special Judge (Sc/St Act)/ Additional District &
Sessions Judge, Farrukhabad in case crime no. 231 of 2022 under Sections 323, 452, 354, 376, 504,
506 I.P.C. and Section 3 (1)da, 3(1)dha and 3(2)va of Sc/St Act, P.S.- Nawabganj, District-
Farrukhabad.

2. Heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as the learned AGA and perused the entire record.
3.

As per prosecution story, the husband of the prosecutrix is engaged in a private job at Noida and his wife, the prosecutrix, lives with her in-laws at village Raipur, P.S.- Nawabganj, district- Farrukhabad.

It was alleged in the FIR that often he uses eve-tease the victim, which was protested by her and after some days the appellant entered into the house of the prosecutrix in the night and Anupam Singh @ Guluwa vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170632759/

sentences.text: On noise made by the victim the other family members and neighbors reached there but the appellant have ran away.
The incident happened in the night on 18.7.2023 and the FIR was lodged on 18.10.2023 after investigation now the charge sheet has been submitted and deposition of some witnesses has been recorded.
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
He has not committed the present offence.
Alleged offences are not attracted against him.
It is further submitted that it is a story of false implication, the appellant is the native of the village of the prosecutrix.
There is no injury cause to the victim of this case and the medical evidence does not corroborate the prosecution version.

It is also submitted that contradictory statements have been made by the victim in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
and in the deposition recorded before the Court during trial.
It is also submitted that he has been falsely implicated by the in-laws of the victim.
It is also submitted that the appellant is languishing in jail since 22.12.2022 and he has no criminal history to his credit and is entitled for bail.
The Court below while passing the impugned order did not take into account the facts and evidence available on record in right perspective and erred in passing the same.
It is lastly submitted that the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant suffers from infirmity and illegality warranting interference by this Court.
5. On the other hand, learned AGA vehemently opposed the appeal and bail application moved by the accused appellant.

6. From the perusal of the record, it appears that there is no material contradiction in the statements made under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and in the deposition recorded before the Court by the victim and a specific role of accused appellant who is the sole accused in this case has been narrated by the victim in her both the statements mentioned herein above.
It also appears from the record that there was no occasion for the prosecutrix to falsely implicate the appellant in such a serious matter.
Prosecutrix of this case is a married lady and to commit rape with her after entering into the house in the night is a grevious offence.
The prosecutrix belongs to a weaker section of the society and is a member of SC/ST community.
There is eye-witness account also and the witnesses have seen the appellant when he was running away from the place of occurrence.
7. I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned order carefully.
8. It appears from the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and from perusal of material on record that the trial court has properly considered the case of the appellant.
Hence, in view of above consideration, the order of rejection of bail passed by the trial court dated 20.02.2024 is affirmed.
9. In the facts and circumstances of the case, I do not find it a fit case to allow this appeal.
10. The criminal appeal is, accordingly, dismissed.
